title: fix: reconcile Z-Image Vast cutover
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Records the single-worker Z-Image fleet with Fal spillover after destroying instance `47267292`.
- Reconciles the six-GPU fixed burn and the completed FLUX RTX 5090 replacement.
- Restores the provider resolver before isolated Z-Image starts when the local DoH helper is stopped.

Root cause: disabling the production tunnel also stopped the local DNS helper, but `resolv.conf` still pointed to localhost, so model startup could not resolve Hugging Face metadata.

Validation:
- `bash -n operations/infrastructure/gpu/zimage/setup-vast.sh`
- 3/3 queue unit tests
- DNS ordering and fleet economics assertions
- Live restart, queue saturation, shared-tunnel generation, production attribution, registry, and fleet health checks

gist.headline: The image hive finds DNS
gist.blurb: Z-Image now wakes up with its map intact: a single Vast worker handles the garden, Fal catches overflow, and the resolver is restored before the first seed is planted.
gist.summary: Reconciled Z-Image onto a single-worker Vast fleet with Fal spillover, completed the FLUX RTX 5090 replacement, and restored DNS resolver setup before isolated Z-Image startup.
gist.impact: Z-Image generation can reliably restart and resolve Hugging Face model metadata even when the local DoH helper is unavailable, while overflow continues through Fal.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy GPU garden where Polli acts as a small systems gardener, reconnecting a glowing DNS path from a retro terminal to a Z-Image worker greenhouse. A friendly CRT monitor robot tends a single sturdy Vast worker machine while a soft pastel Fal cloud catches extra image-seeds drifting overhead; code-plants and flowers signal restored startup reliability.
